messages.subject: ddply examples ?
parts:
Hi Everybody

In light of the results of the plyr survey referred to below. 

I was one of those who responded. I use ldply a lot but hardly ever use ddply. I see in the almost survey everybody uses ddply. I must be missing something because it feels to me that I still haven't figured out the workings (like how do you control the shape of the output dataframe) off ddply its notation (what exactly is the dot? and the brackets). Is there some documentation somewhere on the web that has a more in-depth discussion and examples of how to use ddply and for which types of uses it is particularly suited  (if there was a plyr book like the ggplot book i'll be the first to buy it).

regards
Christiaan

I pretty much only use ddply and ldply and if I understand your question correctly, you can
control the shape of the output dataframe by using 'summarise' inside ddply. Just google
'ddply + summarise' and you will see a few examples. Also, Winston's website has a couple
examples..check it out  http://wiki.stdout.org/rcookbook/Manipulating%20data/Summarizing%20data/

I must be missing something because it feels to me that I still haven't figured out the workings (like how do you control the shape of the output dataframe) off ddply its notation (what exactly is the dot?

"The dot" is a function that looks up column names inside the dataframe using the unevaluated expression vector that is passed to it. You can think of it (possibly) as (something like):

`.` <- sapply( x, function(x) as.character(quote(x))

It's quite a bit like an internal "within". I hasten to add I'm not sure if expression vectors would survive passage through that function definition.
